subject: Pre-QBR: consolidated launch escrow, sprint gating, and mitigation fabric
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-QBR: consolidated launch escrow, sprint gating, and mitigation fabric

Team —

Ahead of the QBR on Friday I wanted to consolidate where we are across the product/eng roadmap and surface the delivery risks we should highlight to execs. This is a concise read — please skim and flag any inaccuracies.

Snapshot (current sprint):
- Core inference runtime: gating on two performance regressions in the 4.1 kernel path (ticket INF-812, INF-834). Regression is seen on long-prefix workloads; perf delta ~12% P50 token latency.
- Model packaging: release candidate for quantized v2 landed last Thursday, still needs canary validation across dedicated pools.
- API surface: streaming stability fix queued; customers on beta reported intermittent truncated streams (support tickets increased by 4x).

Launch windows and constraints:
- Internal target (soft): 2028-05-10 for wider rollout to Hosted API customers.
- Customer milestone (Acme Corp): 2028-05-17 pilot cutoff (they need stable latency for their demo week).
- Hard constraint: Dedicated capacity autoscaler update must be in by 2028-05-08 to avoid SLA exposure for early adopters.

Primary risks (ranked):
1) Performance regression on long-prefix paths (blocks: INF-812/834). If unresolved, we must delay rollout for customers with >2k token prefixes or restrict to quantized v1.
2) Canary validation failure for quantized v2 (data: increased output variance on a small prompt set; root cause likely dequantization path when sequence >1k).
3) Streaming stability (customer-facing; truncated streams harm beta trust).
4) Capacity autoscaler bug under synthetic spike (could cause degraded tail latency for Dedicated pools).

Mitigation proposals (high level):
- Immediate: gating rule — do not promote v2 to general pool until canaries run against a 48-hour production replay; extend canary to 2 dedicated pools.
- Engineering: assign an urgent squad (Rishi, Karthik) to triage INF-812/834; revert to previous kernel path as hotfix if root cause not found within 48h.
- Product/CS: notify Acme of a precautionary contingency (offer a short extension to their pilot date or enable a performance-focused config).
- Ops: prepare autoscaler fallback toggle and ensure manual takeover runbook in Console (Monica).

Asks:
- Vivek: decision on go/no-go criteria we should present to execs (latency SLO delta threshold, canary stability window).
- Rishi/Karthik: confirm squad assignment and ETA for triage plan by EOD Tuesday.
- Monica: readiness of autoscaler fallback with runbook link by Wednesday.

Attachments: launch-checklist-2028-04.xlsx (checklist + gating matrix), qbr-risk-register-2028-04.csv (detailed items).

I’ll synthesize answers and produce a single-slide readout for Friday.

—Marissa
Product Lead, Launch Programs
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: consolidated launch escrow, sprint gating, and mitigation fabric

Thanks Marissa — good, practical summary. A few clarifications from leadership perspective:

1) Go/no-go criteria: propose we present both a hard and soft threshold. Hard = no >10% regression on P95 token latency for production-like traces; soft = P50 delta tolerable up to 8% with documented mitigations and a rollback plan.

2) Exec ask: we want a simple one-slide risk exposure meter (Green/Amber/Red) and a single ask per severity (e.g., extend pilot, accept restricted rollout, or pause).

3) Customer comms: hold off external notifications to Acme until we have the canary replay pass/fail — but prep a short contingency note (Monica/Marissa).

Action items accepted: Rishi/Karthik immediate triage; Monica autoscaler fallback prep. I will join the triage sync if it moves into debugging.

Vivek
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

I spun up a repro for INF-812 this morning using the long-prefix trace set from last week's production capture. Early notes:
- The regression looks tied to a new fused attention kernel activated for sequence lengths >1024 when quantized path intersects with KV cache reuse.
- Root cause hypothesis: an edge-case in the cache pointer arithmetic that increases memory churn and occasionally triggers slower memcpy paths.

Proposed triage plan (48h):
1) Hotfix branch: revert to the prior attention kernel for sequences >1024 and run the 48h production replay across canaries. If P95 is back within threshold, we promote the hotfix + monitor.
2) Parallel investigation: add additional telemetry for cache pointer movement and microbench the memcpy path.
3) Canary validation: expand to two dedicated pools and run both production replay + real traffic sampling for 72h.

I'll take ownership of step 1 and estimate a PR + canary run kickoff by end of day Tuesday (24 Apr EOD). Karthik, can you own telemetry and the memcpy microbench?

If the revert is required and we push a hotfix, it may impact feature parity for sequences >4k until we rework the kernel (estimate 2–3 sprints to fully validate).

Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Marissa —

Autoscaler fallback: I have a manual toggle and an abbreviated runbook ready in the Console. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Prep-Mar-Launch (see file: autoscaler-fallback-runbook.md).

What it does:
- Force-disabled aggressive bin-packing heuristics, revert to conservative slot allocation (adds headroom but increases cost).
- Sets a manual cap on concurrent requests per GPU pool to preserve tail latency.
- Telemetry checks to signal re-enable.

I'll coordinate with Ops to rehearse the manual takeover tomorrow at 15:00 PT.

Monica
Director, Infrastructure Operations
